name: Nested sliding shells (pauldron) + arm ring
verdict: dead: best honest gap 79.46 (reach 0.75, follow 1.00, in-band 14 0.27, contact 0.016) vs the 3R champion 68.93; not worth a GPU sweep. The ring-bearing joints do not remove the 3R family's middle-axis limiter (J2): a revolute concentric with GH must be a surface of revolution, so spreading J2 over a 250 deg ring makes its one radius clear the worst of the arc (about 120 mm vs 61-86 mm along u2). Transferable: a scapula-fixed J1 ring bearing (7 mm stack) sits at one radius of 58 mm, 65-94 % in band - graft it on the champion.
limiter: J2 (middle axis) track: in-band 0.00; its one radius about 120 mm (per-sample q95 64-107, per-pose max to 132 mm at elevation 165 / axial -90 and elevation 60-90 reaches; the ring passes over the bulging deltoid/acromion), and web 2 rides lifted over it (0.00 in band). Second: J3 C-gap loses 22 workspace poses, all at elevation 60-180 (overhead 11 of 13 lost); closing the gap (neck from the ring centre, reach 0.86) sends track 2 to 204 mm, which fails the audit.
